newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle calls ranged from 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.

A weaker tone to cash cattle and boxed beef was expected to prompt carryover selling interest in live cattle futures. Packers were able to purchase fed cattle $1 per cwt lower at $68 late Wednesday and projections of increased fed cattle supplies ahead dshould keep the cash pressured, they said.
Indications on Friday's Cattle-on-Feed report point to larger than year ago on-feed supplies.

Analyst estimates for May 1 on-feed numbers at the seven major feeding areas averaged 109.6 percent and ranged from 108 to 111 percent of last year. Placements averaged 113.9 percent and ranged from 104.9 to 127.5 while marketings averaged 101.0 and ranged from 98.6 to 104 percent.

May feeders were expected to show further strength following another gain in the index and easier corn futures indications. However, back months were expected to show further pressure as fed cattle prices start to slip and concern grows over poor breakeven levels. Feed costs need to drop further, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.13 to $76.10 per cwt, highest level since January 26, 1995.
